transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because I've been having these really difficult thoughts lately. I'm an artist, and recently I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. 

While I was doing it, I just kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. It was like... if I made one wrong photo placement or chose the wrong color, it would mean I didn't actually love her enough. I'm used to second-guessing my work, but I couldn't just brush these off like normal creative doubts. They just kept sticking in my head, and it's been really bothering me.
When those thoughts show up, do you feel driven to do something over and over—like checking, redoing, or arranging the piece a certain way—to make the feeling go down?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens. Um, I'll end up rereading the label text, or... I'll just keep nudging the same objects on my work table. And I'll check the layout photos over and over again until it finally feels, I don't know, "settled" to me. 

Even though a part of me knows it's already fine, I just keep doing it. It's frustrating because I know I'm really just losing good studio time, but I feel like I have to do it until that feeling goes down.
Do these thoughts and repeated checking feel excessive or unreasonable to you?

Yeah, they definitely do. I mean... I know it doesn't make sense. Like I said before, a logical part of me knows the piece is completely fine after the first or second check. 

But I'll still spend all this extra time just nudging a photo a millimeter to the left, and then right back again. It feels excessive because it doesn't actually improve the art at all, it just eats up my day. So, yeah, I know I'm being unreasonable while I'm doing it, but I just have a really hard time walking away until my brain finally gives me the green light.
On a typical day when this is happening, about how much total time do these thoughts and checking rituals take up?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't ever timed it or kept track of the exact minutes. I mean, it definitely interrupts my workflow, but... yeah, I don't really have a specific total time to give you. It just kind of happens in little stretches while I'm at my desk, so it's hard to add it all up.
Would you say these thoughts and checking rituals take more than an hour total in a typical day?

I'm honestly not sure if it adds up to a full hour. Um, like I said, it mostly happens in little bursts, so I don't really know. It might be an hour, or maybe a bit less... I just haven't paid close enough attention to the clock to say for sure.
Have these thoughts and checking rituals noticeably interfered with your work or daily life?

Yeah, it has. I mean, I'm still getting most of my work done, for the most part. But... the extra time I lose in the studio because of all this checking, it's starting to have an impact. 

Like, it actually cost me a grant deadline recently because I just couldn't finish the portfolio in time. And... I even had to back out of a gallery talk that I really wanted to do, just because I was so behind and stressed about it. So, yeah, it is definitely interfering.
Do these unwanted thoughts and checking rituals happen only when you’re working on the memorial piece for your aunt?

I haven't really noticed if it's just tied to that one piece, to be honest. I mean, I've been working on the memorial a lot lately, so it definitely happens then, but... I'm not sure if it *only* happens with that specific project. I just haven't really kept track of whether it happens with my other pieces too.
Did these thoughts and checking start after your aunt died?

I'm not entirely sure. I mean, I know things have been pretty stressful since she passed, but I can't say for certain if that's exactly when all this started. It might have been around then, or... maybe a little before? I just haven't really pieced together a clear timeline of when it actually began.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself and the time I'm losing to all this checking, but... I haven't really felt down or depressed most of the day. It's really just been more about the stress of falling behind on my work.
Outside of your artwork, do you find yourself worrying a lot about several other parts of your life?

Not really. I mean, I have normal everyday things I think about, like anyone else, but... I wouldn't say I worry a lot about a bunch of different areas of my life. Almost all of my stress right now is really just focused on my artwork and all the checking I've been doing.
Have you had these same unwanted thoughts and checking rituals while working on artwork that has nothing to do with your aunt?

No, it's really just the portrait of my aunt. I haven't had these thoughts or felt the need to check like this with any of my other pieces. It seems to be entirely focused on this one specific project.
Did these thoughts and checking begin within 3 months after your aunt died?
Um, I'm actually not sure. I didn't really... keep track of the exact timeline like that. So I couldn't say for certain if it started specifically within that three-month window.
Before your aunt died, had you ever had this same kind of unwanted thought-and-checking problem?

No, never. I mean, I've always been a little particular about my art, just wanting it to look right, but... nothing like this. This whole thing with the unwanted thoughts and the constant checking, it's completely new. It only started with this portrait.
When you stop working on the portrait of your aunt, do the unwanted thoughts and checking go away?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't... I haven't actually put it away long enough to find out. I mean, even when I take a break for the evening, the project is still kind of hanging over me, so I'm usually still thinking about it. I couldn't tell you if the thoughts would completely stop if I just stopped working on the portrait altogether.
Do these thoughts and checking feel mainly connected to your grief about your aunt’s death?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I am grieving, of course, but the thoughts aren't really about missing her or feeling sad. It's just... this intense focus on getting the portrait exactly right, and the fear that if I don't, something bad will happen. It doesn't feel like it's about the grief itself.
